instruction: Use command line tools to crop the image to 800x600 pixels starting from the top-left corner and save it as "cropped.png" on the Desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey("ctrl", "alt", "t"); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires cropping the tilearray.png image to 800x600 pixels from top-left corner. Evaluator checks if the output image has exactly 800x600 dimensions. Original image is 962x1280, so this is a valid crop operation.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts image dimensions from the output file using PIL
Metric correctly compares actual dimensions against expected 800x600 values
Expected values correctly reflect the instruction requirements (800x600)
Handles edge cases appropriately (missing file, None results, invalid dimensions)
Parameter handling is correct: metric receives rules dict directly when expected.type='rule'
Minor limitation: Does not verify that crop started from 'top-left corner' (only checks dimensions), but verifying pixel content would be impractical without comparing to original image
File existence at '/home/user/Desktop/cropped.png' is implicitly verified by the getter attempting to read it
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding comparison with original image to verify crop position if pixel-level accuracy is critical, though this significantly increases complexity
Current approach (dimension-only check) is a practical and reasonable verification for this task
